[Glasgow · 26–27 November 2026]{.eyebrow}

# RSE-hackathon

Two days of building an **open RSE learning environment** — and other research software engineering tools — in **Glasgow**.

[Register on Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/rse-hackathon-2026-at-university-of-glasgow-tickets-2000034040655){.cta target="_blank"}
:::

::: {.hero-body}
Research Software Engineering (RSE) practice and training remain fragmented along disciplinary lines:
each field reinvents tooling, conventions, and teaching material, so we will conduct an open hackathon to prototype discipline-overarching RSE frameworks
— shared, reusable building blocks that work across the social sciences,
life sciences, and the humanities rather than within a single silo.

## The flagship idea: an RSE learning environment

RSE teaching material is plentiful and much of it is excellent. A shared environment in which learners
actually _work_ is not. Oxford RSE's [Gutenberg](https://www.rse.ox.ac.uk/gutenberg) gets furthest —
open source, with accounts, courses and progress tracking — but the loop between learners is still open
everywhere: group formation, submitting an artefact, getting feedback, reviewing someone else's code.
So learners read about good practice instead of practising it on each other's code.

::: {.why-grid}

::: {.why-card}
### Notebooks, not pages
Traditional learning environments (Moodle, Canvas, ILIAS) were built for self-contained documents and
quizzes. They cannot host a Jupyter or R Markdown notebook as a first-class, runnable assignment.
:::

::: {.why-card}
### Real compute, not toy examples
RSE assignments need the machines RSE actually runs on: [GPUs, batch schedulers, HPC allocations,
containers]{.highlight}. No LMS can embed an exercise that has to be submitted to a cluster.
:::

::: {.why-card}
### OER in, OER out
What learners and instructors produce should leave the platform again as open educational resources —
as notebooks and as [standards-described learning objects]{.highlight}, not locked in a course shell.
:::

:::

### The challenge for the two days

A minimal working example of the pipeline: simple user management, group formation, a feedback loop,
and peer assessment for uploaded RSE artefacts.

We use a thin-slice approach: rather than spending the two days building a complete database or UI,
we connect just enough of each layer to show a user interacting with a real, working feature — alongside
an overall system design (UML or similar) to carry the work forward.

[Standards, architecture and the open questions →](learning-environment.html){.people-link}

A breakdown into modules that a single team can take on in two days, and what we think the two days
can realistically produce, is on the [modules page](modules.html).

Other ideas for projects and prototyping are of course more than welcome!

## Practical information
The hackathon takes place at [University of Glasgow, Scotland]{.highlight} on the 26th and 27th of November, 2026 at the [advanced Research Centre]{.highlight}
at _University of Glasgow, 11 Chapel Lane, G11 6EW_.

_Day 1:_ lightning talks framing the challenges, team formation, and prototyping (09.00 to 17.00)

_Day 2:_ build a short showcase and a community roadmap for carrying winning prototypes forward. (09.00 to 17.00)

Hybrid attendance for remote contributors is also possible.

Join the conversation on our [Matrix room](https://matrix.to/#/#rse-hackathon-glasgow-:matrix.org).
:::

The coolest module gets an award and stiped.

<button id="theme-toggle" class="theme-toggle" aria-label="Toggle light and dark mode">● Dark mode</button>
<script>
(function () {
  var root = document.documentElement;
  var btn = document.getElementById('theme-toggle');
  var stored = localStorage.getItem('theme-v2');
  function setDark() {
    root.setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
    btn.textContent = '☀ Light mode';
  }
  function setLight() {
    root.removeAttribute('data-theme');
    btn.textContent = '● Dark mode';
  }
  if (stored === 'dark') setDark();
  btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var isDark = root.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark';
    if (isDark) {
      setLight();
      localStorage.setItem('theme-v2', 'light');
    } else {
      setDark();
      localStorage.setItem('theme-v2', 'dark');
    }
  });
})();
</script>
